title: Cloud Connector traffic forwarding
aliases: where does cloud connector send this traffic

prose.text: {{purpose}} "Where did Cloud Connector send this flow?" is answered in the order below.

steps.label: Which rules apply to this Connector and flow?
steps.text: Scope by location or Connector group, then services, sources and destinations; FQDN criteria need the workloads' DNS to pass through the Connector: [[cloud-connector.forwarding.criteria]].

steps.label: In what order are rules evaluated?
steps.text: Ascending rule order with disabled rules holding their slot; whether the first match ends evaluation is open: [[cloud-connector.forwarding.rule-order]], [[cloud-connector.forwarding.rule-order:first-match]].

steps.label: What does its method do?
steps.text: ZIA, ZPA, Direct, Drop or Local, and how they appear in the API: [[cloud-connector.forwarding.methods]].

steps.label: Did a predefined rule handle it?
steps.text: The default Internet & SaaS rule, the Private Access rules and the gateway-mode Direct rules: [[cloud-connector.forwarding.predefined-rules]].

prose.text: For ZIA-method traffic, the tunnels to the Service Edges and what happens when they fail: [[cloud-connector.overview.gateway-failover]].

Two other policies run beside traffic forwarding: DNS policies and gateways ([[cloud-connector.dns]]), and Log and Control Forwarding for the Connector's own logs and control traffic ([[cloud-connector.forwarding.log-and-control]]).

ZIA's Forwarding Control is a separate policy in a different product: [[zia.forwarding-control]]. Terraform behavior of these rules: [[cloud-connector.terraform.forwarding-rules]], [[cloud-connector.terraform.rule-order]], [[cloud-connector.terraform.delete-detach]].

purpose.statement: Traffic Forwarding forwards selected traffic to specific destinations: through Internet & SaaS or Private Access, bypassing them for a portion of workload traffic, or dropping selected workload traffic, configured as rules.

quotes: Traffic Forwarding enables you to forward select traffic to specific destinations based on your needs.
Give granular control of traffic forwarding from cloud locations to Internet & SaaS or Private Access.
Grant the user the ability to bypass Internet & SaaS or Private Access for a portion of workload traffic.
Allow the user to prevent traffic forwarding and drop selected workload traffic.
use the traffic forwarding method by configuring appropriate rules.
